Pinned upstream direct runner scale-set client; API and listener interfaces inspected at v0.4.0.
Hybrid architecture; v1 standalone ephemeral VMs; Kubernetes hosts control plane and VMs need not join it.
Companion to ARC, no fork by default; use supported boundaries and separate ownership.
Per-runner policy abstraction; lowest-price initially; future expected-cost/risk policies remain extension points.
Ordinary GitHub runs-on targeting logical scale set; no custom workflow syntax.
Resource requirements plus portable hard constraints and soft preferences, not mandatory provider-specific machine names.
Search spot across all allowed clouds/regions; optional explicitly enabled cheapest eligible global on-demand fallback.
Direct GitHub Runner Scale Set Client/API in v1, with execution backend abstraction for future ARC/Kubernetes-native execution.
Multiple named provider configurations; external credentials through Kubernetes Secrets/workload identity; no credential material in runner CRDs.

Spot-interruption retries are opt-in and disabled by default. When enabled, confirmed interruption permits a fresh bounded GitHub rerun, acknowledging dependent-job reruns and possible repeated external effects; temporarily exclude/deprioritize failed capacity source, without migration. Exact lineage and placement mechanism remain open.
Minimum vCPU/memory with optional architecture/vendor/performance-class requirements. Initial supported subset must be declared.
Explicit Docker, privileged-container, nested-virtualization and accelerator capabilities; disposable isolation does not eliminate capability checks.

Provisioning waits/retries until its persisted configurable deadline. At expiry, report local provisioning timeout, stop new creation for that expired attempt and retain cleanup obligations. GitHub retains queue and terminal-result authority; do not fail the job or cancel its workflow merely because the local deadline expired. Subsequent admission/rearming policy remains to be specified.

Adopt explicitly recommended defaults unless materially ambiguous or no defensible recommendation exists. This does not authorize construction. Construction is separately authorized by AUTH-UBUNTU-001.
Use aggregate scale-set demand, with in-flight provisioning counted, rather than incrementing capacity per event. GitHub selects jobs within the compatible scale set.

Exhaustive means coverage of every eligible pool in a finite catalog snapshot for a search round. Record attempted, unavailable, cooling-down, unknown and unvisited pools separately; never call a partial round exhausted.

Hard constraints, denied regions and configured maximum prices never become soft during retries or fallback. Unknown required capability is ineligible; unsupported requested features yield explicit validation status.

For v1 lowest-price, rank eligible VM compute hourly rates in one declared currency at a recorded snapshot; disk, network and interruption costs are separate disclosed estimates. Never label this cheapest total job cost.
Cloud-create timeout means commitment unknown. Reconcile by durable operation identity before reissuing creation; retain cleanup obligations across controller restarts.
Recovery cannot depend on receiving an interruption warning. Reconcile provider state; unknown runner loss does not itself prove spot interruption.
Persist linked records in JSON with stable IDs and explicit provenance; plan JSON Schema 2020-12 validation plus cross-reference checks. No harness validator is built in this phase.
Companion owns its own scale sets and VM resources. ARC and companion must not concurrently reconcile the same scale set.
Project name is RunneScout; filesystem/repository slug is runnescout. Preserve the user spelling rather than substituting RunnerScout.

Explicit Ubuntu handoff and subsequent scoped approval authorize development, harness/product construction and GitHub repository artifacts in tsouza/runnerscout. Sandbox and review controls remain enabled. No production or unbounded cloud spending. Canonical name RunnerScout.
Implementation target in target.md; BASE-0002 remains partial. Local verification does not establish live integration.

Go 1.27.1, actions/scaleset v0.4.0, Kubernetes 1.37, Ubuntu 24.04 amd64/arm64 and AWS/Azure/GCP are the current development matrix. Helm uses maintained v3.22.0. Live paths and arm64 remain unqualified; dependency-status.md records compatibility exceptions.

Use namespace-scoped ConfigMaps with resourceVersion CAS and a Kubernetes Lease for the first controller. One dedicated class and scale set per deployment. ConfigMaps are actual persistence, not a CRD API.

An unchanged demand cohort cannot silently replenish expired admissions. Confirmed terminal job completion plus observed VM deletion releases successful slots. Zero demand and confirmed cleanup permit a new cohort.

Opaque scale-set job IDs remain distinct from numeric REST IDs. Retry guard requires one terminal failed REST job matching runner name, workflow run and attempt, confirmed provider interruption, acknowledgment and a bounded lineage. Live rerun execution is not yet implemented.

Compare integer USD microdollars per VM compute hour, at most five minutes old, within an explicitly complete finite allowed-pool snapshot. Disk, egress and tax excluded. Automatic discovery/refresh remains tracked implementation work.
Use the MIT License for the open-source project, adopted as a permissive default under the standing recommendation authority.

Local diagnostic evaluation is serialized and bounded to 60 invocations and six evaluator hours, ten minutes per invocation. It does not enforce total agent wall time or provide independent evaluator custody. Preserve failed/incomplete evidence; no CI pass implies live integration.

The initial CI scan rejected Go 1.26.2, x/net v0.52.0 and x/text v0.35.0. Update to Go 1.26.7, x/net v0.55.0 and x/text v0.39.0; retain the failed scan and require passing fresh scans. Use Node 24 GitHub Actions revisions.
Azure belongs in the provider target alongside AWS and GCP. The earlier two-provider implementation scope was an agent assumption, corrected by the user. No Azure exclusion is retained.

Use local cloud emulators for the next API-integration stage, without paid cloud accounts. Ministack 1.5.10 covers EC2; Floci Azure 0.12.0 covers mocked VM control-plane APIs. Floci GCP currently lacks standalone Compute Engine instances. Keep emulator, fixture and live-cloud claims distinct; no emulator substitutes for the final real-VM matrix.
EC2 API metadata mode and optional container execution; pinned image used for isolated adapter tests.
VM control plane is mocked. Its official az-vm CLI compatibility test is best-effort and may skip; RunnerScout must not interpret that as full adapter support.

maxRunners is a mutable admission ceiling during Helm upgrades. Lowering it admits nothing above the new ceiling and retains existing allocations, deadlines and consumed slots until normal cleanup/reset. Other class/provider identity fields remain immutable. Fleet binding v2 omits only maxRunners; old bindings migrate only when all other fields match a valid previous bounded limit.

Sweep remaining development PRs through required checks to merge; keep dependencies and third-party libraries current across the project and cache Go dependencies across CI runs. No bypass of repository or sandbox controls.

After the dependency/CI/PR sweep, implement the Kubernetes CRD configuration surface and comprehensive schema-validated worked examples for every CRD, including AWS/Azure/GCP providers, runner requirements, placement/fallback, retries, credentials and ordinary runs-on workflows. The current ConfigMap-only runtime does not satisfy this request; no example may imply unimplemented behavior.

Expose an opt-in uniform logical private-network option spanning AWS VPC, Azure VNet and GCP VPC. Keep separate provider networks as default. Start qualification locally using isolated network domains and a real overlay, with positive/negative connectivity, DNS and ephemeral cleanup checks; real cloud routing remains separately unqualified until bounded authorized tests. No paid network provisioning is authorized by this option request.

Build a release pipeline for tested same-commit versioned multi-architecture images and packaged Helm charts, checksums, SBOMs, signatures/provenance and release notes. Require qualification and security gates, a verifiable promotion path and rollback guidance; do not create a 0.1.0 release before the full requested acceptance is proven.

Release promotion must reject regressions. Require bug-reproducing tests, accepted-baseline behavioral/API/CRD compatibility, Helm upgrade/rollback and preserved-state checks, provider/end-to-end qualification and security gates. Missing, skipped, stale, failed or inconclusive required evidence blocks publication. Never rewrite expected results automatically or treat the partial discovery baseline as an accepted release.

The experimental runnerscout.io/v1alpha1 API uses namespaced ProviderConfig, RunnerClass, RunnerScaleSet, CapacityCatalog and NetworkProfile resources. Derive cloud resource owner from scale-set identity; provider references are reusable. Resolve only same-namespace dependencies and verify stable UID/resourceVersion snapshots. Generated schemas and compiler tests do not imply runtime reconciliation or supported shared-overlay/retry execution.
